messages:
maya: quick Q — where's the best dashboard to check prefix/KV cache hit-rate for app-ingest? Alerts kept paging last night, trying to triage.
sam: grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/cache-overview?orgId=1&var-service=app-ingest — open the 'KV prefix hitrate' panel and the heatmap for seq-length distribution.
maya: thanks. any quick links for traces/logs if I want to find specific requests that missed the cache?
sam: traces: https://traces.redwood.example/trace?service=ingest&tag=kv_prefix_miss — filter by span.name=serve_prefix to see where miss happened. for logs use Loki with LogQL, e.g.:
```
{job="ingest"} |= "kv_prefix_miss" | json | route="/v1/generate" | duration_ms > 50
```
that narrows noisy chatter.
kevin: FYI the alert is `kv_cache_low_hitrate` — it fires when 5m avg < 0.6 for service=app-ingest. We might want to lower to 0.55 or increase the `for:` window to 10m to reduce flapping. Also consider a deploy exemption for 30m.
maya: do we have per-prefix hitrate panels? need to see if a few hot keys are driving global stats down.
sam: yes — panel called 'hitrate by prefix (top 50)'. Query we use: `topk(50, sum by (prefix) (rate(kv_prefix_hitrate_sum[5m]) / rate(kv_prefix_hitrate_count[5m])))` — or use `kv_prefix_miss_total` grouped by prefix for absolute misses. can add table view if helpful.
kevin: also check eviction metric: `kv_cache_evictions_total`. if evictions spike, hitrate drop is expected. And check prefetch success rate: `kv_prefetch_success_ratio`.
observability-bot: Alert config snapshot: kv_cache_low_hitrate — threshold: 0.6, eval_interval: 1m, for: 5m. Current state: firing (app-ingest).
maya: runbook?
sam: runbook here: https://wiki.redwood.example/runbooks/kv-cache.md — follow 'investigate low hitrate' steps: dashboards, traces, prefetch config, recent rollouts.
maya: ok i'll follow those and open a PR to temporarily lower the threshold to 0.55 + add a 30m mute during deploys. pinging @kevin for approval :eyes:
kevin: ack, I can review. also add an annotation on the grafana panel for last deploy (helps correlate). :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — i'll post findings in this thread when I have them.
